assessments.evidence: Port city in a province with no active armed-group territorial control; PNC commissariats handle policing, arrests and order, with FARDC/naval units garrisoned in the city. Crime (kuluna) and past Bundu dia Kongo unrest did not amount to territorial control. No sources could be retrieved in this run.

units.CD2002-boma: Boma, a city-territory and port on the lower Congo River in Kongo-Central, lies far from the eastern conflict zones and no armed group holds territory there. Day-to-day order in all its health-area neighbourhoods is kept by the Congolese National Police (PNC), with FARDC and naval forces (Boma hosts a Force Navale presence on the river) also stationed in the city. Security issues are urban crime (kuluna-type banditry) and past political unrest linked to the Bundu dia Kongo movement (notably 2017-2020), which did not displace state control. Web research was unavailable for this run (search budget exhausted), so the assessment rests on default state presence.
